rapport_notes: Warm, patient, uses customer's name, acknowledges details, builds collaborative tone throughout—'Look at you. Look at that up. Great!'
process_discipline_notes: Rep did not hold silence after the open-ended agenda question (customer started to answer, rep acknowledged immediately without pause); rep ended call without explicit rate-lock or close-ask line, and without silence buffer after 'does that feel fair' equivalent.

evidence_quotes.agenda: Before we get too far in, are there any like, concerns or just important questions that you have top of mind that I can just kind of dive into first.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Rep probed pickup location access deeply ('are there two different elevators?', 'where would the truck be parking?', 'how far from truck to elevator?', 'how far from elevator to unit?', 'will you be able to reserve the freight elevator?') and destination similarly ('what part of the building?', 'are we going through patio or front door?', 'if cars are parked, where would truck park?'). Customer raised 'confusing address' concern upfront; rep clarified with multiple follow-ups until fully documented.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: You only pay for the time you use any like regardless so while... if we, if we say we're increasing it but they actually end up it ends up taking them less time than we thought I would only pay for the last time... Yes, you are correct, you are correct. [Estimate window:] Originally the system had you fitted for about three to four hours we're gonna need to increase that for sure... to about six and a half, about two and a half more hours. Because we really don't know about the first location just yet like if we're gonna fit and even if we do fit we still have quite a bit of walk from the truck to the elevator.

top_strength: Exceptional two-layers-deep probing on both pickup and delivery logistics; rep asked clarifying follow-ups on parking, elevator access, and distance repeatedly until every scenario was mapped, and documented all contingencies for the crew.
coaching_note: Four of five Save Your Ass lines are missing (commit-to-rate experience, self-prep tip, does-that-feel-fair, and the close rate-lock/ask), and neither damage coverage nor Meet Your Mover differentiator was ever surfaced—these must be delivered in Stage 2 as takeaway or Stage 1 if customer raises them; rep also skipped the quid pro quo framing and closed without an explicit ask or rate-lock statement.
